CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypertension and palpitations

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old male with hypertension since young age. Recently presented to emergency room in March with elevated blood pressure and palpitations. Patient attributes this episode to consumption of several cups of coffee on an empty stomach and believes it may have been a panic attack. He has not experienced palpitations since that time. Recently started on new antihypertensive medication approximately one month ago by new primary care physician. Checks blood pressure at home daily with current readings ranging from 146-155 systolic, not yet at goal. Attempting to reduce salt intake. Exercises on treadmill when possible. Currently on three antihypertensive medications at maximal doses.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies abdominal pain. Denies lower extremity edema.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension (since young age)

MEDICATIONS
1. Amlodipine 10 mg daily
2. Benicar HCT 40-25 mg daily (started approximately one month ago)
3. Spironolactone (newly prescribed)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Multiple family members with hypertension

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient attempts to reduce dietary salt intake and exercises on treadmill when possible.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal
Pulmonary: Lungs sound good
Abdomen: Soft, no tenderness to palpation
Extremities: No edema in ankles or feet

RESULTS
Serum potassium (one week ago): 4.0 mEq/L
Thyroid profile from March 1, 2021: To be copied forward from prior records (specific values not discussed)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Resistant hypertension on three maxed-out antihypertensive medications. Started spironolactone. Discussed potential side effects of spironolactone and hydrochlorothiazide including electrolyte abnormalities, dehydration with dizziness upon standing, and rare gynecomastia (approximately 1 in 100 males). Baseline serum potassium of 4.0 provides adequate room to safely initiate spironolactone. Counseled patient on dietary modifications including salt restriction to less than 2000 mg/day (recommended goal 1500 mg/day) and increased potassium intake. Recommended DASH diet plan. Advised on importance of regular exercise, noting potential reduction of 7 to 10 points in blood pressure with 30 minutes of treadmill walking most days of the week. Provided patient education resources including American Heart Association website (heart.org) and DASH diet information. Discussed complications of uncontrolled hypertension including cardiac enlargement, heart failure, kidney failure, and stroke. Scheduled follow-up appointment in two weeks for blood pressure check and metabolic panel to monitor potassium and sodium levels. If inadequate response to spironolactone, will refer to resistant hypertension clinic for evaluation of secondary causes and consideration of procedural interventions such as renal denervation.
